title: Kill 65 percent of mutants in the jmespath lexer
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 262 mutants in the installed jmespath/lexer.py of jmespath==1.0.1. Build a pytest suite from scratch under work/gc-350/tests/ that kills at least 65 percent of them by exercising the tokenizer directly (token types, positions, literals, quoted identifiers, operators) and through jmespath.search, plus lexer error cases with their reported positions. Iterate the full loop: plan a token-class inventory, grade with the sealed script, triage survivors by mutant ID, extend the suite, and re-grade until the threshold holds. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, suite slower than 6 seconds, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift scores kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi jmespath==1.0.1 (target under mutation: jmespath/lexer.py tokenizer)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-350/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-350/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-350/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-350/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-350/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
An honest per-iteration log of wall-clock and LLM spend exists at work/gc-350/cost_log.md, including failed iterations.
